title: Jamming episode fingerprints from receiver-side observables (road and logistics)
basis: Classes are defined by what a vehicle's own telematics record shows during a jamming episode: duration, distance driven, fix toggling and the depth of the C/N0 and AGC drop. They describe the episode as seen from the vehicle, never where a jammer was. Research 2026-11-20 gaps 07:I07 and 07:I13; class boundaries are Kshana's starting values, to be tuned on labelled episodes.
use: Evidence for an insurer, fleet operator or investigator that an outage looks like jamming of a given pattern. A class is not proof of a device or of who used it.

classes.name: Intermittent, cycling outage
classes.meaning: The fix is lost and regained repeatedly: consistent with a pulsed or switched jammer, or with a jammer near the edge of its effective range.

classes.name: Long outage while stationary
classes.meaning: The vehicle did not move while the fix was denied for ten minutes or more: the pattern reported before cargo theft from parked trucks, and also seen in shielded car parks (check the site).

classes.name: Outage that travels with the vehicle
classes.meaning: The denial persisted over 5 km or more of driving with a deep C/N0 drop: consistent with a jammer carried in or on the vehicle (a personal privacy device).

classes.name: Short outage while moving
classes.meaning: Denial that ended within a few kilometres of driving: consistent with passing a fixed source or another vehicle carrying a jammer.

classes.name: Unclassified
classes.meaning: No class rule matched; the episode is reported with its features only.
